(a) in mmWave networks, the rate increases with the BSs density, (b) the cell edge rate increases faster than the median rate, and (c) self-backhauling can be used to guarantee the same QoS with different BS densities.

mmWave systems can provide higher cell-edge spectral efficiency than conventional UHF cellular networks with the same BS density and can provide the same median cell-edge rate as UHF networks at a lower BS density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental rate trends of self-backhauling mmWave cellular networks and the associated design tradeoffs.
the fundamental tradeoff between rate, BS density, and the fraction of BS with wired backhaul.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mmWave cellular systems with high-gain directional antenna arrays and self-backhauling are a promising solution to enable dense deployments in future 5G cellular networks.
mmWave cellular networks with self-backhauling are more resilient than conventional UHF cellular networks.

, in a mmWave cellular network with directional antennas and self-backhauling: (i) the median cell edge rate scales as the BS density to the power of 2/3; (ii) increasing the BS density increases the median cell edge spectral efficiency; (iii) increasing the bandwidth boosts the median and cell edge rates; and (iv) the cell edge rates are insensitive to the wired backhaul density, while the median rate is sensitive to the wired backhauling density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mmWave cellular networks with self-backhauling are expected to be more robust than conventional UHF networks against BS density variations, and the median rate is insensitive to the system bandwidth.

mmWave cellular systems are not only interference-limited, but they also exhibit a unique combination of coverage and capacity trends that can be exploited to design efficient and flexible cellular systems with self-backhauling.
, in contrast to UHF cellular systems, mmWave cellular networks with self-backhauling have an increasing median cell edge rate as the BS density increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given QoS, the BS density can be traded off with the wired backhaul requirement, which is a key parameter for the network design and planning.
, with self-backhauling and directional antennas, mmWave cellular systems can support a high BS density without compromising the QoS.
, in mmWave networks with self-backhaul, the BS density is a key system parameter that can be used to achieve a desired rate distribution.
